h1: Alpe d'Huez ski resort, stays & events guide
heroText: Alpe d'Huez sits on a sunny plateau at 1,827 metres with more than 250 kilometres of slopes above it. The Sarenne drops 16 kilometres without a break, which the resort calls the longest black slope in the world, and the old village of Huez lies down the hairpins below.
stayOverview: The resort itself is up on the plateau with the lifts; Huez village is cheaper down the hairpins; Oz and Vaujany are satellites on the same pass.
hotelIntro: Book against high season. Staying on the plateau means walking to the lift; staying below means driving the twenty-one hairpins twice a day.
rentalCars: The road up is the twenty-one-hairpin climb the Tour de France uses. Grenoble is the nearest city and airport transfers run in winter.
